fields.name: dns1
fields.fieldText:
PUBLIC DNS If the phone's provisioning counter is not moving up, this indicates that the phone is having a hard time connecting to the Internet. This usually indicates a problem with the DNS server the phone is connecting to. Set the phone to connect to a Public DNS by accessing the web interface and going to:
  • Settings
  • Network
  • Ethernet
Set the DNS Server to use publicly known DNS server such as:
  • Google: 8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4
  • Verizon: 4.2.2.2, 4.2.2.3
Do not forget to save the settings before rebooting the device.

There might be an issue on the network, ports and firewall security, DHCP settings and RingCentral server that needs to be investigated by a Tier2 specialist. Before Escalating do the following. 1. fields.name: checklist
fields.fieldText:
Checklist: Before you start following this guide, please ensure that ALL of the following information have been checked:
  • User/Extension Status
    • Must be “Enabled”.
    • Extensions on “Not Activated” state should be set to “Enabled”.
  • Serial Number
    • Check for duplicates (not removed).
    • Duplicate serial numbers listed to other accounts must be removed. Please get assistance from your Team Lead to clear this.
    • If no duplicates can be found, ensure that the Serial Number is associated with the DIGITAL LINE number.
  • Phone Model
    • See table below for list of supported models for more information kindly see article number 3619 or click the link Deskphones - List of Supported Phones | RingCentral Retired models are no longer supported and should be provisioned manually.
    • Ensure that the correct model number is associated with the DIGITAL LINE number.
  • Billing Status
    • No failed billing on Digital Line numbers.
    • Check the status of the Digital Line Number associated to the Device by going to Admin Interface > Phone Numbers(find the Digital Line and check the status beside it sample (205) 415-4527 Change # ) it should be "Change". Charge status means the DL failed to be charge and will cause registration issues and the phone unable to be provisioned on our RingCentral provisioning server. To rectify this click on the #charge status to manually charge the Digital Line.
  • Device Certificate
    • Must be “Factory Installed”.
    • Devices that are “Self-signed” will only work via manual provisioning, these devices are considered defective and should follow the RMA process when applicable. To check Device Certificate on the phone menu go to Menu > Status > Product Information (Use arrow keys go down to DEVICE CERTIFICATE)
  • Firmware
    • For SPIP phones - 4.0.9
    • Refer to RC 411 News Update No 1620 version 3 - RingCentral : Polycom Phone Firmware Upgrade (VVX and SPIP Model)
    • For VVX phones - 5.6.0
    • Refer to RC 411 News Update No 1634 version 3 - RingCentral : Polycom Phone Firmware Update (VVX Model) - Firmware version. VVX Polycom Model Old Firmware - 5.4.2.6722 New firmware - 5.6.0 Please follow the troubleshooting guide on updating the phone's firmware via the phone's built-in software update tool.
  • Internet Access
    • Ensure that the customer has Internet access.
  • Device Status
    • Phone should be turned on with the correct light indicators (see light indicators on Success and Google for specific models)
    • ICS "Internet Connection Sharing" is not recommended. Internet Connection Sharing is a Windows service that enables one Internet-connected computer to share its Internet connection with other network enabled device on a local area network (LAN). The computer that shares its Internet connection serves as a gateway device, meaning that all traffic between other computers and the Internet go through this computer.
NOTE: In the event that you get roadblocked when using this guide, please ask assistance from a Team Lead.

fields.name: CHECKDHCPSTATUS
fields.fieldText:
CHECK DHCP STATUS If the phone is getting an IP Address of 0.0.0.0, this indicates that the phone has an invalid IP Address and is considered not getting an IP Address at all. Isolate the problem by checking the DHCP Client:
  • Check the physical connection and ensure that the ethernet cable is connected to the correct ports on both the network source and the phone.
    • The ethernet cable should be plugged in to the LAN port of the phone, otherwise it will show an error stating "Network link is down"
    • The light on the corresponding port on the router/switch where the phone is connected should lit up indicating a "link" between the 2 devices.
    • It is always best to try a known good port on the router/switch and also a known good cable to isolate connectivity issues.
  • When applicable, perform a sequential reboot from the router then the switch.
    • Rebooting the network devices refreshes any IP conflict within the network that could be causing the phone to not get a valid IP Address.
  • Check the DHCP status of the phone and ensure that the "DHCP Client" is enabled.
    • Check the DHCP status by going to: Menu> Status> Network> TCP/IP Parameters

  • Gain agreement from the customer to leave the case open for 24hrs to monitor the phone behavior.
  • Gather all important information

fields.name: phoneinterface
fields.fieldText:
OPEN PHONE'S USER INTERFACE If you're unable to access the web interface of the IP Phone, isolate the problem by trying the following:
  • "https://" instead of "http://" before the IP Address.
  • Trying a different browser.
  • Please also check if the web interface is enabled Menu > Advance > Administration Settings > Web Server Configuration. Web Server = YES
  • Ensuring that the phone is connected to the same network as the computer. - Plug the phone directly to the router where the computer is connected to. - Make sure the default gateway of the phone is the same as the default gateway of the computer trying to access the GUI(Graphical User Interface) of the phone. Note (Default gateway is the IP address of the Router/Switch). Follow the steps below for the step by step process in getting the default gateway of the phone and computer.
  • For Polycom - Setup - Settings - Menu> Status> Network> TCP/IP Parameters (look for - - Default Gateway)
  • For Windows - Click on Start button and choose All apps. - Find app Search, type command cmd. Then click on Command Prompt (you can also press WinKey+R and enter command cmd). - Type ipconfig /all and press Enter. Find the Ethernet adapter Ethernet, locate row Default Gateway.
  • For MAC
1. Launch “System Preferences” and click on “Network” icon 2. Select the active network interface from the left side menu that you want to uncover the Gateway address for 3. Now click on the “Advanced” button in the lower right corner of the Network preference panel 4. Click on the TCP/IP tab 5. Find the gateway address next to “Router:” in the format of an IP address, like so: x.x.x.x IMPORTANT: If the default gateway of the phone is different from the default gateway of the computer trying to access the GUI of the phone it means the two device are connected on different router/switch. Ask the customer to have the phone connected to the same network as the computer trying to access the GUI of the phone or vice versa. Refer the customer to their IT personnel if they are unable to connect the phone or the computer on the same network. Note: Ensure that ALL the above steps have been isolated before moving forward.

fields.name: refertoisp
fields.fieldText:
REFER TO ISP/NETWORK ADMINISTRATOR Refer the customer to their network administrator or their ISP to check why the phone is not acquiring an IP Address. A few of the common reasons could be due to the following:
  • The DHCP Server of the router is disabled In the event that it is disabled, the phone must be supplied by a Static IP Address consisting of the following:
    • IP Address
    • Subnet Mask
    • Default Gateway
    • DNS Server Address
  • The router/switch has advanced security options that may "block" unknown devices from acquiring a valid IP Address until such time that the MAC Addresses are added to the "trusted list"
Note: In the event that the customer is also the network administrator, walk the customer through in checking the above options.

TIER 2 ESCALATION Issue is the mismatch with Instance ID's of the old and new devices in Admin Interface. Inform the customer that a ticket will be sent to tier 2 to rectify the issue with our back end tool with regards to the device unique ID's. Reminders before escalating the case:
  • Gather all important information

fields.name: TypicalPhoneIssueScenario
fields.fieldText:
This guide will help you to troubleshoot in provisioning or registering your LOCKED POLYCOM IP phones. Please utilize the steps of troubleshooting under this guide to provide the best possible solution to your caller. SELECT THE TYPE OF ISSUE THAT IS BEING EXPERIENCED
  • NO IP ADDRESS - The phone IP Address is equivalent to 0.0.0.0. It means that the phone is not connected to the network. To check if the phone is getting an IP Address please go to the phone Menu > Click Setup Key > Status > Network Status > TCP/IP - IP phones need to acquire IP address from a DHCP server. If the DHCP server in a network is not available, any devices connecting to it will not be able to automatically acquire an IP address. (Ex. Phone has no IP or the IP address is 0.0.0.0 / 169.254.x.x)
  • PHONE OFFLINE - The phone is offline on the online account under Phones and Devices. - VoIP connection depends on an active and stable internet connection. - If the connection is unstable, or completely down, the desk phone won’t be able to communicate with the RingCentral servers. Ex. of common errors URL Disabled, Time and Date out of Sync and No dial tone.
  • INTERMITTENT REGISTRATION - The phone loses its registration intermittently to our RingCentral server as well as to the customer's network.
  • RETURN CALLS FOR OBSERVATION - Returned calls after being advise to observed the connection for 24hrs.
  • CHECK STATUS or CHECK IN PROGRESS - This is not a provisioning error. It is a status of the device on the online account for first time setup.

VALIDATE INSTANCE ID Validate if the device to be registered(new device) has the correct Source InstanceID(old device) and the old device has the correct Target InstanceID(new device). What to do: 1. Open the customer's Admin Interface > Go to Phones and devices (Look for the old device and new/replacement device) 2. Make sure the following are matched.

  • Target InstanceID - This refer to the new device Instance ID, the old device should have same Target InstanceID(Highlighted in Blue)
